entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Carlos Ibáñez e Ibáñez de Ibero, 1st Marquis of Mulhacén, was a Spanish divisional general and geodesist. He represented Spain at the 1875 Conference of the Metre Convention and was the first president of the International Committee for Weights and Measures. As a forerunner geodesist and president of the International Geodetic Association, he played a leading role in the worldwide dissemination of the metric system. His activities resulted in the distribution of a platinum and iridium prototype of the metre to all States parties to the Metre Convention during the first meeting of the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1889.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ibáñez de Ibero's leadership in the metric system led to its global dissemination, influencing scientific and industrial practices worldwide. His efforts resulted in the establishment of a platinum-iridium prototype of the metre, distributed among Metre Convention member states, solidifying his impact on international measurement standards.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Carlos Ibáñez de Ibero's leadership in the dissemination of the metric system led to its global adoption, with the distribution of a platinum and iridium prototype of the metre to all Metre Convention states parties by 1889. This achievement had significant regional impact on Spain and Latin America.
